LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERN

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern, part of Strand 3 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we use correct sentences in our speech or writing? 2. How can we write sentences correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. use the target language pattern in sentences correctly for fluency in speech,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. respond to questions on the language patterns in written communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. adopt the use of language structures for effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. use the target language pattern in sentences correctly for fluency in speech,

   Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. respond to questions on the language patterns in written communication,

   Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. adopt the use of language structures for effective communication.

   Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. recite a poem with the pattern enough + nominal + infinitive and a lot/a lot of... related to the theme with peers,

2. identify lines from the poem that have the language patterns enough + nominal + infinitive and a lot/a lot of....,

3. construct sentences using the language patterns enough + nominal + infinitive and a lot/a lot of... with peers,

4. complete a written exercise based on the language patterns enough + nominal + infinitive and a lot/a lot of.... 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. recite a poem with the pattern enough + nominal + infinitive and a lot/a lot of... related to the theme with peers,
2. identify lines from the poem that have the language patterns enough + nominal + infinitive and a lot/a lot of....,
3. construct sentences using the language patterns enough + nominal + infinitive and a lot/a lot of... with peers,
4. complete a written exercise based on the language patterns enough + nominal + infinitive and a lot/a lot of.... 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: This is promoted as the learner is able to make own sentences using appropriate

language patterns correctly.

● Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner gains confidence to recite poems before peers.

Values:
● Respect: This is promoted as the learner is able to appreciates other’s contributions when working to identify lines from

the poem that have language patterns.

● Integrity: This is enhanced as the learner is able to demonstrate commitment to tasks both individually and when

working with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peaceful coexistence: It is promoted as the learner is able to interact and socialise with peers harmoniously when working on

tasks.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of language structures with their learning of similar concepts in Kiswahili.

2. respond to questions on the language patterns in written communication,
3. adopt the use of language structures for effective communication.
